A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PISCES study. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite additions and layout shifts.

before.justification: v1 reports original concept-erasure experiments on Gemma and Llama, including benchmark results, relearning attacks, feature analyses, and human validation of the answer judge.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds feature-selection agreement results, a difference-in-means experiment, and statistical comparisons.

M1.justification: Appendix G adds a supervised difference-in-means implementation: derive concept directions from retain/forget activations, select vectors by cosine similarity, and apply weight orthogonalization. The principal SAE-based PISCES procedure remains unchanged.

E1.justification: The eleven concept domains, concept and similar-domain questions, MMLU, AlpacaEval, and relearning/adversarial scenarios are retained. The new disentangler and agreement studies reuse existing concepts and feature-selection coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds an evaluated difference-in-means comparator for Gemma in Appendix G and Table 3. RMU, ELM, MEMIT, and AlphaEdit already appear in v1's comparisons; Section 5's correction from 'three' to 'four' does not add those baselines.

E3.justification: New Appendix A.3 introduces a four-annotator agreement protocol using five sampled concepts per model and 158 candidate features. Appendix G evaluates the alternative disentangler across all concepts on Gemma. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, generation limits, and hyperparameter-search settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds two focused analyses: agreement on manual feature filtering and an alternative-disentangler experiment testing the SAE implementation's advantages. Existing feature-quality correlations, computational-cost analysis, and adversarial evaluation remain intact.

E5.justification: v1 already reports confidence intervals and statistical tests for feature correlations and judge validation. v2 additionally reports Fleiss' kappa for feature selection and paired t-tests comparing PISCES with ELM and RMU across five Gemma metrics. No increased run or seed count is stated.

E6.justification: Original benchmark values and plotted results are unchanged. New Table 3 reports difference-in-means accuracy of 28.7 ± 4.4, AlpacaEval of 54.8 ± 6.4, and relearning accuracy of 44.2 ± 6.1. Appendix A.3 adds kappa = 0.574, and Table 4 adds comparative significance results.

T1.justification: Appendix G introduces the difference-vector definition, the corresponding disentangler, and the weight-orthogonalization update in Equation 6. The original framework assumptions and Equations 1–5 are unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about precise parameter-level concept erasure, the SAE implementation, modest efficacy gains, and improved specificity and robustness. The appendix additions support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix G newly interprets the alternative's lower relearning accuracy as accompanying damaging edits, rather than establishing a better overall tradeoff. Appendix H adds a significance-based interpretation, although Table 4 shows no significant similar-domain difference against RMU (p = 0.36). Existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix G documents activation collection from retain/forget data and reuse of concept-encoding layers for the new variant, although its top-k setting is unspecified. Existing SAE hyperparameters, data-generation instructions, code disclosure, packages, and H100 hardware information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds REVS to the unlearning discussion, Rimsky and Arditi references for the supervised variant, and Fleiss and Landis–Koch references for agreement analysis. Core research positioning is unchanged. The additional AxBench bibliography entry duplicates an already cited work.

P1.justification: The main narrative receives limited clarifications and corrections, including the comparator count. Appendix A.3 and Appendices G–H are added, moving Resources and Packages from G to I. There is no extensive rewriting or reorganization of the existing argument.

P2.justification: v2 adds two compact tables for difference-in-means performance and paired tests. Original Tables 3–5 become Tables 5–7, and several appendix displays shift position. All nine original figures and their content are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical support through agreement measurement for subjective feature filtering, a useful alternative-disentangler comparison, and paired significance tests. These address gaps in v1 while preserving its main evidence. The gains are limited: agreement is moderate, the alternative's top-k setting remains unspecified, and significance does not extend to every comparison.
